tools.name: create_asset_link
tools.title: Create Asset Link
tools.description:
Mints a new permanent share link for an existing Grunt chart or table asset, identified by assetId (returned by chart/table creation tools). Every creation tool already auto-mints one 'view' link, so you normally only need this tool for two cases: getting an additional view link, or getting an 'edit' link.

The returned assetUrl is a permanent JSON manifest source with a pinned commit. Follow links.svg.href for the image, links.export.href for objects, or links.data.href for values; edit manifests also advertise links.project.href for the complete Grunt model. Preserve the permanent source URL in saved artifacts. Append desired width/height only to the source request.

permission:
- 'view' (default): read-only. Grants the FULL read surface -- the rendered image, the raw SVG, and the underlying data values, not just the picture.
- 'edit': read/write. Required for embedding a chart into a PowerPoint deck via the grunt-pptx skill, so the Grunt add-in can load the complete model for local editing in the deck. This does not convert it into a built-in PowerPoint chart or automatically publish deck edits to the cloud.

Norm for edit links (PowerPoint / artifact embedding): mint ONE FRESH edit link per asset per generated artifact. Reuse it for repeated placements of that asset within the same artifact; mint a new link for a different artifact. Each link grants access to the whole asset; separate links allow an asset owner to revoke one artifact's access without disabling other links.

Links have no automatic expiry. An authorized asset owner can revoke individual links. Treat every minted link -- especially edit links -- as a capability that remains valid until revoked or the asset is deleted. Prefer 'view' unless the caller specifically needs to modify the asset in place.

assetId.description: The unique identifier of the chart or table asset to create a share link for.

permission.description: Permission granted by the link: "view" (read-only, default) or "edit" (read/write; use for PowerPoint embedding). (Default value: "view")

tools.name: create_or_update_area_chart
tools.title: Create or Update Area Chart
tools.description:
Creates or updates an area chart for emphasizing magnitude and volume over continuous data. Similar to line charts but fills the area below the line, making it ideal for showing cumulative totals, volume changes, or stacked contributions over time.

Data format: 2D table where:
- Header row: [Empty, Point A Name, Point B Name, ...]
- Data rows: [Series Name, Point A Value, Point B Value, ...]

Area charts are particularly effective when:
- Showing part-to-whole relationships over time (stacked areas)
- Emphasizing the total volume or magnitude of change
- Visualizing cumulative data

Updates existing chart if assetId provided; creates new chart otherwise. Changing chart types (different tools, orientations, or bar/line types) requires a new assetId.
NOTE: Changing between area/area100 requires that no assetId is provided so a new asset is created.

Indexing: categoryIndex/seriesIndex selectors in annotations, rules, and pointColors use full-dimension indexes: zero-based positions in the full chart data dimensions, including header rows, label columns, and other non-plotted dimensions. Do not renumber plotted data to data-only ordinals. With the table layout above, the first plotted category and first visible series are usually index 1, not 0. Per-series arrays such as seriesColors, lineDashStyles, lineThicknesses, markerShapes, and markerSizes are different: they use zero-based rendered series order.

Annotations: Pass overlays through the tool's `annotations` property. Supported types for area: `line`, `jump`, `level`, `callout`; for area100: `line`, `level`, `callout`. CAGR is not supported on area charts.

Color schemes: Use settings.colorScheme to apply a predefined color scheme (check slide context for available schemes). Prefer colorScheme over manually picking seriesColors when a predefined scheme fits the user's request. Both can be combined: colorScheme sets the base palette and seriesColors overrides specific series on top.

Number format: The numberFormat property on labels accepts Excel-style format strings or preset names.
If omitted, the chart type's default format is used (e.g., Percentage for 100% stacked charts).
Presets: 'General', 'Number' (#,##0), 'Percentage' (0%), 'Currency' ($ 0.0), 'Accounting' ((#,##0.0)), 'Year' (0000), 'Multiple' (0.0x), 'Absolute' (0;0).
Common formats: '0%' → 25%, '0.0%' → 25.3%, '#,##0' → 1,234, '$#,##0.00' → $1,234.56, '0.00' → 25.30.
Magnitude: Append k, m, or b to divide by thousands, millions, or billions. The letter only scales the number and prints nothing; to show a suffix, add it as a quoted literal after the letter (e.g., for 1,234,567: '#,##0.0k' → 1,234.6; '#,##0.0k"k"' → 1,234.6k).
Flags (space-separated after format): neg(parentheses|minusSign|absolute) zero(dash|empty|zero).
Scientific notation (E+/E-) is not supported.

Returns: assetId and assetCommit for subsequent modifications, a PNG screenshot of the rendered chart, and an export URL. May include warnings about data validation issues.

tools.title: Create or Update Combined Chart
tools.description:
Creates or updates a combined chart mixing bar/column and line series in a single visualization. Ideal when you need to compare data on different scales or show relationships between metrics of different types (e.g., sales volume as bars, profit margin as a line).

Data format: 2D table where:
- Header row: [Empty, Category A Name, Category B Name, ...]
- Data rows: [Series Name, Category A Value, Category B Value, ...]

Each series can be configured independently as either bar/column or line type. Supports:
- Dual Y-axes for different value scales
- Clustered or stacked bar arrangements
- Multiple line series overlaying bars

Use cases:
- Revenue (bars) vs. profit margin percentage (line)
- Volume (bars) vs. growth rate (line)
- Actual values (bars) vs. targets or trends (line)

Updates existing chart if assetId provided; creates new chart otherwise. Changing chart types (different tools, orientations, or bar/line types) requires a new assetId.
NOTE: Changing between vertical/horizontal/stacked/clustered/stacked100 requires that no assetId is provided so a new asset is created.

Indexing: categoryIndex/seriesIndex selectors in annotations, rules, pointColors, and lines use full-dimension indexes: zero-based positions in the full chart data dimensions, including header rows, label columns, and other non-plotted dimensions. Do not renumber plotted data to data-only ordinals. With the table layout above, the first plotted category and first visible series are usually index 1, not 0. Per-series arrays such as seriesColors, lineDashStyles, lineThicknesses, markerShapes, and markerSizes are different: they use zero-based rendered series order.

Annotations: Pass overlays through the tool's `annotations` property; supported annotation types include `cagr`, `line`, `jump`, `level`, and `callout`.

Color schemes: Use settings.colorScheme to apply a predefined color scheme (check slide context for available schemes). Prefer colorScheme over manually picking seriesColors when a predefined scheme fits the user's request. Both can be combined: colorScheme sets the base palette and seriesColors overrides specific series on top.

Number format: The numberFormat property on labels accepts Excel-style format strings or preset names.
If omitted, the chart type's default format is used (e.g., Percentage for 100% stacked charts).
Presets: 'General', 'Number' (#,##0), 'Percentage' (0%), 'Currency' ($ 0.0), 'Accounting' ((#,##0.0)), 'Year' (0000), 'Multiple' (0.0x), 'Absolute' (0;0).
Common formats: '0%' → 25%, '0.0%' → 25.3%, '#,##0' → 1,234, '$#,##0.00' → $1,234.56, '0.00' → 25.30.
Magnitude: Append k, m, or b to divide by thousands, millions, or billions. The letter only scales the number and prints nothing; to show a suffix, add it as a quoted literal after the letter (e.g., for 1,234,567: '#,##0.0k' → 1,234.6; '#,##0.0k"k"' → 1,234.6k).

Creates or updates a line chart for visualizing trends and continuous data patterns. Best for showing changes over time, growth rates, or trajectories. Use when you want to emphasize the flow and continuity between data points.

Data format: 2D table where:
- Header row: [Empty, Point A Name, Point B Name, ...]
- Data rows: [Series Name, Point A Value, Point B Value, ...]

Each row becomes a separate line on the chart. Line charts are ideal when the order of points matters and there's a logical progression (typically time-based). For discrete categorical comparisons, use bar charts instead.

Updates existing chart if assetId provided; creates new chart otherwise. Changing chart types (different tools, orientations, or bar/line types) requires a new assetId.
NOTE: Changing between line/index requires that no assetId is provided so a new asset is created.

Indexing: categoryIndex/seriesIndex selectors in annotations, rules, and pointColors use full-dimension indexes: zero-based positions in the full chart data dimensions, including header rows, label columns, and other non-plotted dimensions. Do not renumber plotted data to data-only ordinals. With the table layout above, the first plotted category and first visible series are usually index 1, not 0. Per-series arrays such as seriesColors, lineDashStyles, lineThicknesses, markerShapes, and markerSizes are different: they use zero-based rendered series order.

Annotations: Pass overlays through the tool's `annotations` property; supported annotation types include `cagr`, `line`, `jump`, `level`, and `callout`.

Color schemes: Use settings.colorScheme to apply a predefined color scheme (check slide context for available schemes). Prefer colorScheme over manually picking seriesColors when a predefined scheme fits the user's request. Both can be combined: colorScheme sets the base palette and seriesColors overrides specific series on top.

If omitted, the chart type's default format is used (e.g., Percentage for 100% stacked charts).

Data format: 2D table where:
- Header row: [Category, Value]
- Data rows: [Category Name, Numeric Value]
Example: [["Category", "Value"], ["Product A", 100], ["Product B", 150], ["Product C", 75]]

Chart types:
- 'pie': Traditional filled circle divided into slices
- 'donut': Ring chart with hollow center (allows for central labels/totals)

Supports features like rotation angle, slice explosion (pulling slices out), and various label placements. Note: Avoid pie charts when comparing many categories or when precise value comparison is needed - bar charts are better for those cases.

Updates existing chart if assetId provided; creates new chart otherwise. Changing chart types (different tools, orientations, or bar/line types) requires a new assetId.

Indexing: categoryIndex/seriesIndex selectors in callout annotations, rules, rotation.seriesIndex, and explode use full-dimension indexes: zero-based positions in the full chart data dimensions, including header rows, label columns, and other non-plotted dimensions. Do not renumber plotted data to data-only ordinals. With the [Category, Value] data layout above, the first plotted slice is usually seriesIndex 1 because row 0 is the header. sliceColors is different: it is an array in zero-based rendered slice order.

Annotations: Pass overlays through the tool's `annotations` property. Supported annotation type: `callout` only.

Color schemes: Use settings.colorScheme to apply a predefined color scheme (check slide context for available schemes). Prefer colorScheme over manually picking sliceColors when a predefined scheme fits the user's request. Both can be combined: colorScheme sets the base palette and sliceColors overrides specific slices on top.

If omitted, the chart type's default format is used (e.g., Percentage for 100% stacked charts).

tools.description:
Creates or updates a scatter or bubble chart for visualizing relationships between variables and distributions. Ideal for showing correlations, clusters, outliers, or patterns in multi-dimensional data. Scatter charts plot points based on two variables (X, Y); bubble charts add a third dimension via point size.

Data format: 2D table where:
- Header row: [Label, X, Y, Size, Group]
- Data rows: [Point Label, X Value, Y Value, Bubble Size, Group Name]

Points sharing the same Group value are rendered as a single series with consistent styling. The Size column determines bubble diameter (use consistent values for standard scatter chart).

Use cases:
- Correlation analysis (relationships between two variables)
- Distribution patterns and clustering
- Outlier detection
- Multi-dimensional data visualization (bubble size as 3rd dimension)

Updates existing chart if assetId provided; creates new chart otherwise. Changing chart types (different tools, orientations, or bar/line types) requires a new assetId.

Indexing: categoryIndex/seriesIndex selectors in rules use full-dimension indexes: zero-based positions in the full chart data dimensions, including header rows, label columns, and other non-plotted dimensions. Do not renumber plotted data to data-only ordinals. groupColors is different: it is an array in zero-based rendered group order. Scatter/bubble pointColors use rowIndex, an explicit zero-based data-row index where the first data row is 0.

Annotations: Not currently supported on scatter/bubble charts. Do not include the `annotations` property.

Color schemes: Use settings.colorScheme to apply a predefined color scheme (check slide context for available schemes). Prefer colorScheme over manually picking groupColors when a predefined scheme fits the user's request. Both can be combined: colorScheme sets the base palette and groupColors overrides specific groups on top.

Number format: The numberFormat property on labels accepts Excel-style format strings or preset names.
If omitted, the chart type's default format is used (e.g., Percentage for 100% stacked charts).
Presets: 'General', 'Number' (#,##0), 'Percentage' (0%), 'Currency' ($ 0.0), 'Accounting' ((#,##0.0)), 'Year' (0000), 'Multiple' (0.0x), 'Absolute' (0;0).
Common formats: '0%' → 25%, '0.0%' → 25.3%, '#,##0' → 1,234, '$#,##0.00' → $1,234.56, '0.00' → 25.30.
Magnitude: Append k, m, or b to divide by thousands, millions, or billions. The letter only scales the number and prints nothing; to show a suffix, add it as a quoted literal after the letter (e.g., for 1,234,567: '#,##0.0k' → 1,234.6; '#,##0.0k"k"' → 1,234.6k).
Flags (space-separated after format): neg(parentheses|minusSign|absolute) zero(dash|empty|zero).
Scientific notation (E+/E-) is not supported.

Returns: assetId and assetCommit for subsequent modifications, a PNG screenshot of the rendered chart, and an export URL. May include warnings about data validation issues.

tools.description: Create or update a Grunt table, also called a Visual Grid in Grunt: an editable, formatted data table that can go on a PowerPoint slide as a Grunt object, not a plain PowerPoint table. This is Grunt's table tool, for any table the user wants, including to insert or add one on a slide: a data, comparison or financial table, scorecard, KPI matrix, dashboard grid, or table visual encoding (conditional fill/font/style, icons, gauges, shapes, flags, logos/images, sparklines/chart-in-cell). Input: a TableDefinition with `cells` for new tables and optional `settings` for formatting, conditional rules, graphics, merges, sizing, and row/column/cell scoped overrides; pass `assetId` to update an existing table. For a settings-only update to an existing connected table, omit `cells` to preserve its source and cached values. Side effects: creates or updates the remote table asset and may add warnings when requested resources cannot be resolved. Returns asset identifiers, export/download links, warnings, screenshot content, and svg/project metadata. Optimization: prefer global settings (e.g., `numberFormat`, `font`, `alignment`) combined with `modifierScopes` to target specific columns or rows, rather than repeating the same setting across many `cellStyles` entries. Use `columnStyles` or `rowStyles` when an entire column or row shares the same formatting. Reserve `cellStyles` for truly cell-specific exceptions. Observed behavior: nested `numberFormat` settings merge with outer scopes (not full replacement), conditional rules are evaluated top-to-bottom and first matching rule wins, and applying multiple graphic modifiers to the same cell can overlap or override so one graphic modifier per cell is safest. Scientific notation (E+/E-) is not supported in numberFormat. For image/logo fields (`simpleImage`, `conditionalImage`, `logo`), pass an existing image resource key/hex key/name or a cloud logo identifier/search term.

tools.name: create_or_update_waterfall_chart
tools.title: Create or Update Waterfall Chart
tools.description:
Creates or updates a waterfall chart to visualize sequential cumulative effects. Perfect for financial analysis showing how an initial value is impacted by positive and negative changes to reach a final total. Ideal use cases include profit/loss statements, budget variances, inventory flow, or any step-by-step accumulation.

Data format: 2D table where:
- Header row: [Empty, Step A Name, Step B Name, ..., Total Name]
- Data rows: [Series Name, Step A Value, Step B Value, ..., Total Indicator]

Numeric cells are incremental changes, INCLUDING the final column. A label such as 'Total' does not change a bar's role. To create a calculated total extending from the baseline, use:
- lowercase 's': Auto-calculate sum of this series only
- uppercase 'S': Auto-calculate sum of all series (use in only one series)
- Example: headers [Empty, Start, Increase, Decrease, Total], series [Value, 529, 267, -49, 's'] produces a closing total of 747. Putting 747 in the final cell adds another 747, ending at 1494.

Each bar shows the incremental increase or decrease, connecting to show the cumulative flow from start to end.

Updates existing chart if assetId provided; creates new chart otherwise. Changing chart types (different tools, orientations, or bar/line types) requires a new assetId.
NOTE: Changing between vertical/horizontal requires that no assetId is provided so a new asset is created.

Indexing: categoryIndex/seriesIndex selectors in annotations, rules, pointColors, and connector definitions use full-dimension indexes: zero-based positions in the full chart data dimensions, including header rows, label columns, and other non-plotted dimensions. Do not renumber plotted data to data-only ordinals. With the table layout above, the first plotted category and first visible series are usually index 1, not 0. Per-series arrays such as seriesColors are different: they use zero-based rendered series order.

Annotations: Pass overlays through the tool's `annotations` property; supported annotation types include `line`, `jump`, `level`, and `callout`. CAGR is not supported on waterfall charts.

Color schemes: Use settings.colorScheme to apply a predefined color scheme (check slide context for available schemes). Prefer colorScheme over manually picking seriesColors when a predefined scheme fits the user's request. Both can be combined: colorScheme sets the base palette and seriesColors overrides specific series on top.

Number format: The numberFormat property on labels accepts Excel-style format strings or preset names.
If omitted, the chart type's default format is used (e.g., Percentage for 100% stacked charts).
Presets: 'General', 'Number' (#,##0), 'Percentage' (0%), 'Currency' ($ 0.0), 'Accounting' ((#,##0.0)), 'Year' (0000), 'Multiple' (0.0x), 'Absolute' (0;0).
Common formats: '0%' → 25%, '0.0%' → 25.3%, '#,##0' → 1,234, '$#,##0.00' → $1,234.56, '0.00' → 25.30.
Magnitude: Append k, m, or b to divide by thousands, millions, or billions. The letter only scales the number and prints nothing; to show a suffix, add it as a quoted literal after the letter (e.g., for 1,234,567: '#,##0.0k' → 1,234.6; '#,##0.0k"k"' → 1,234.6k).
Flags (space-separated after format): neg(parentheses|minusSign|absolute) zero(dash|empty|zero).
Scientific notation (E+/E-) is not supported.

Returns: assetId and assetCommit for subsequent modifications, a PNG screenshot of the rendered chart, and an export URL. May include warnings about data validation issues.

To refresh a connected chart's values, or to point it at a larger or another range, read the range again from the workbook, new rows included, and send those values as data together with this dataImportDefinition: its filePath and the range they fill. Pass the range's current values as the data. On an update of a connected chart or table, a filePath and range sent with newly read values refresh the connection, and point it at that workbook and range. Never a path in a sandbox or container, such as a copy of an attached file. Omit only when the session has an attached Excel workbook (Grunt's in-app chat); elsewhere a range without filePath cannot connect a chart or table.

tools.name: deck_insert_asset
tools.title: Insert Grunt Asset Into Deck
tools.description:
Places a Grunt chart or table, by the assetId a create_or_update_*_chart tool or
create_or_update_table returned, on one slide of a presentation (deck) open in the user's PowerPoint, as
an editable Grunt object. The asset's newest version is placed; when assetCommit names an older
one, the result carries a desktop_asset_commit_stale warning. The placed object is a copy:
updating the asset afterwards leaves the slide as it is, and placing the new version with
replaceObjectKey, the old copy's objectKey, puts it in the old one's place, legends included.
A Grunt chart or table already on a slide that this conversation did not make changes the same
way: make it again with its create_or_update_* tool, from the data deck_read_slide summarizes and
without an assetId (an objectKey is not one), and place that with replaceObjectKey.
bounds, in points from the slide's top-left corner, set the object's position and size; without
them it takes the replaced object's place, where its shape is now, or keeps its own size, scaled
down to fit a smaller slide, centred across the slide and a little below its middle, where Grunt
puts a new object. It takes the presentation's theme. Put the slide's headline and text on first:
another tool's text edit can replace the slide, and the placed object then gets a new objectKey.
A chart with a separate legend is placed together with its legend, as two Grunt objects; bounds are
then those of the two together, and at a size other than the asset's the legend keeps its own size
and its side of the chart, so its labels do not wrap, and the chart takes the rest. Any other asset
of more than one Grunt object is refused with desktop_asset_not_single_object.
The insert applies immediately, as one PowerPoint undo step, the replacement included. The result
names the presentation, the new object's objectKey and where it landed, each legend placed with
it in legends, and replacedObjectKey; objects lists what was created and deleted.

they are connected to: Grunt reads each workbook on the user's computer and applies its current values,
as the user does with Update in Grunt. Use it when the user asks to update, refresh or sync connected data,
or has changed a connected workbook. A create_or_update tool changes only the asset, which is a copy, not
the object placed in the deck.

object on that slide, or neither for every connected object in the presentation. The values belong to the
workbook source, not the object: every object connected to the same source is updated with it, on any slide,
and is listed as updated. Tell the user when that reaches objects they did not name. The result lists each
object updated, already current, or not updated and why: a workbook that is missing, cannot be read, or is
not an Excel workbook. Grunt reads a workbook as it is open in Excel, or else as last saved; one on a
network share, or one that can contain macros (.xlsm, .xlsb, .xls), is read only while it is open in Excel.

change and formatting stays; a title or other text written from the old values stays as it was.

tools.name: register_local_excel_connection
tools.title: Connect a Chart or Table to a Local Excel File
tools.description:
Finds an Excel workbook on the user's computer and reads a range of it, through Grunt in the user's
PowerPoint, so that a chart or table made from it stays connected to that file. Saving the workbook does
not change the chart or table: Grunt in PowerPoint shows that new data is available, and the user applies
it with Update, or you do with deck_update_data. Tell the user that. Use it whenever the user wants a
chart or table from an Excel file of theirs kept connected, linked or updating.
Give filePath when the user named the workbook by its full path. For a workbook the user attached to this
chat, which you have only as a copy (such as /files/input/Sales.xlsx), give its fileName and the SHA-256
of that copy, computed in code execution from the file's bytes: Grunt looks for the original among the
workbooks open in Excel and in the user's Desktop, Documents, Downloads and OneDrive folders, and takes
the one with the same contents. The copy's name can differ from the original's, as when spaces become
underscores, which Grunt allows for; when you know the original name, such as from the user's message,
give that. Without sha256 nothing is read: the workbooks of that name are listed for
the user to choose. When none matches, the error says what to ask the user. Either way, a workbook on a
network share, or one that can contain macros (.xlsm, .xlsb, .xls), is read only while it is open in Excel.
range is a worksheet-qualified A1 range such as 'Sales Q1'!B2:D8, or a named range, header row
included, of at most 10,000 cells; read the copy first to choose it.
Returns data and a dataImportDefinition that names the file: pass both unchanged to a create_or_update
chart tool (for create_or_update_table, data.values are its cells.values), then place the asset with
deck_insert_asset. To refresh such an asset, or extend its range, read the range again with this tool and
pass the result with its assetId. Reads the workbook through Excel and changes neither the workbook nor
the deck.
